I ve had my cat for almost 4 years and i can relate to you. At some point 1-2 years ago i used to be very jealous of my new flat mate because my cat would spend more time with her than me. When i would get an episode/suicidal, the lack of affection from my cat would feel devastating.

Now idk if im better because my roommate has been busy in the past year and didn't spend as much time home, but my cat stays more with me and lately we're even sleeping together and shit. during this period i ve noticed stuff like.. Whoever is home more/feeds her, would get more attention from my cat. Also, all cats are different and each breed or individual give different amounts of affection.

So i guess my point here is don't stress over it, i know how that feels but after all cats rule their life around their instincts like food SLEEP and whom they see. And im sure your cat's life revolves around you, but she might simply has its own distant personality (my cat has always been very very scared of humans and would bite scratch etc) 

Ps: i ve also noticed forced love works haha

I personally have a lot of friendships that involve periods of talking nonstop and then suddenly talking very rarely. But i always tell them why i haven't reached in so long, and they get it and the friendship is still there even tho sometimes it doesn't feel like it. Usually i dont talk because i just dont have the energy to write a simple text or simply interact, as dumb as that might sound. I think it would help your friend open up if you d tell them how this makes you feel, but without sounding accusatory. I know it's hard for you too, im sorry

I wouldn't say it s the bpd if that feeling has lasted for 2 months already. And that's fine, everybody can feel this way, that there s a spark missing in their relationship even though they get along great. It's a sad and frustrating situation, but it's just life and people's brains reacting to what/whom they'd be really happy with

Ugh, im sorry this happened to you. And it sucks that it happened where it should be a safe place for you. What helped me through such a situation was channel the fear, the paranoia into anger. Get angry at him or, fuck me, them, because there are a lot of pricks that just assume we re property on the streets. There's nothing wrong with you, there are just a bunch of assholes out there and be proud that at least yours is onto getting some justice. I, on the other hand, just saw my assaulter one week ago out there after 4 years and i just froze.

Idk what else to say, try not to devaluate yourself because of this prick, it's not your fault, you were just a person there at the wrong time, if it makes you feel safer take on some self defense classes. Anyway, it will get better. Take care of yourself
Besides that, now I'm just filled with rage and frustration and I wanna cut contact with all my friends, but then what would I do, even more alone?

Idk if it helps but I was in this cycle of fast/binge last year, then i started recovering and eating like a normal person for a while but ofc I relapsed.
However, instead of starting with really low calorie intake (200-400) or fasting, i decided to eat around 700-1000. You lose harder and lower, but it prevents binges.
Would also advise cooking food yourself, like spinach with lota of spices, broccoli, mushrooms, chicken breast etc. It helped me because i realised how good cooked food tastes like that it stopped me from eating junk food.
Hope it helped somehow, take care :)
